decisions.rationale: distinct_count 10760 on id equals dataset row_count 10760 with null_rate 0.0, so runway_id (cast from id) uniquely identifies each row and is declared the grain.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 10760, so no exact-duplicate handling is required.

surface has 239 distinct values (e.g. 'ASP','ASP-G','ASP/CONC') and is documented as a non-fixed code list, so it is renamed surface_code per the operator's code-naming convention without enumeration.

low_end_displaced_threshold_feet (null_rate 0.884) and high_end_displaced_threshold_feet (null_rate 0.900) are highly sparse but retained nullable since most runway ends simply lack a displaced threshold.
Per operator naming conventions, le_/he_ prefixes and ft/deg/degt unit suffixes were spelled out to low_end_/high_end_ and feet/degrees/true_degrees across the runway-end geometry columns.

purpose: This table provides one cleaned row per runway from OurAirports, capturing runway identity, physical dimensions, surface type, lighting and closure status, and the low-end and high-end geometry of each runway, feeding runway- and airport-level analysis when joined to the airports table.
usage: Consumers should treat runway_id as the unique key, join to the airports table via airport_id or airport_ident, and expect frequent nulls on the low-end/high-end latitude, longitude, elevation, and heading columns (roughly 22%-28% null) and on the displaced-threshold columns (88%-90% null); do not assume these are populated, and filter or coalesce explicitly where completeness matters.
limitations: Cleanup did not resolve the high null rates on low_end/high_end latitude, longitude, elevation, and heading (about 22%-28%) or on displaced-threshold columns (88%-90%); surface_code remains an open, non-enumerated code list per the publisher's own documentation and was not validated against a fixed vocabulary; length_feet and width_feet keep their source DECIMAL(38,9) precision rather than being narrowed to integer despite integral sample values.
